title: Image edits handle large inputs more predictably
summary:
Image editing and Gemini thinking requests got more predictable, while publishable-key docs and a community app link got tidied up.

GPT Image editing now downscales inputs whose area exceeds 1536 × 1536 pixels while preserving their aspect ratio, and chooses the closest supported output aspect ratio. Image-generation requests also avoid charges when a successful HTTP response contains text or JSON instead of media.

Gemini 2.5, 3 Flash, and 3 Pro thinking settings now use Portkey-compatible parameters. Requests can set `thinking_budget` directly or use a `thinking` object; zero-budget requests are translated according to what each model supports.

The docs now label publishable keys Alpha, show `?key=YOUR_KEY` in the query-parameter example, and describe the limit as 1 Pollen per hour per IP and key. This updates guidance, not rate-limit enforcement.
